about: Local-LLM task pack for Liquid Dock. run_tasks.py sends each task's prompt (prompts/common_rules.md + the task prompt + its context) to the model, saves the answer under out/<id>/ and verifies it. C++ test tasks are built and run, then run against deliberately broken copies of the code under test ('mutants'): a good test notices most of them. Keep the 'find' strings in sync with src/ (run_tasks.py --self-check tells when one no longer applies).

context.title: tests/fluent_logic_test.cpp (the existing test: do not repeat it, add to it)

mutants.desc: FluentOrder puts the primary monitor last instead of first
FluentOrder orders the other monitors from right to left
MonitorForSetting treats the setting as 1-based (setting 1 gives the first monitor instead of the second)
SettingNumber returns 0-based numbers (the primary monitor gets 0 instead of 1)
PrimaryOf returns -1 for a non-empty list without a primary monitor (should be 0, the first monitor)
WantedMonitor lets the settings file win when shownAt == fileAt (the shown monitor should win a tie)
WantedMonitor ignores fileMonitor 0 from the settings file (falls back to the primary monitor and Reason::Default)
Steady still holds 'nothing playing' back when exactly `hold` seconds have passed (it should switch at now - offSince == hold)
Steady does not restart the hold when 'playing' comes back for a moment (off at 0, on at 1.0, off at 1.2: at 1.6 it already switches to not playing)
StillWaiting is still true at exactly kRehomeSeconds (3.0 s) after the loss
StillWaiting is true for lostAt = -1 (nothing lost) when now is small
Steady::Waiting() stays true after the hold has passed and value became false

context.title: tests/fluent_settings_test.cpp (the existing test: do not repeat it, add to it)

mutants.desc: Trimmed keeps trailing tabs, \r and \n (only spaces are trimmed at the end)
XmlText decodes & first, so "&lt;" becomes "<" instead of the text "<"
XmlText no longer decodes '

mutants.find: std::wstring open = L"<" + name + L">", close
mutants.desc: Element matches the opening tag without its '>' (so <NameX> counts as <Name> and the text gets a stray '>')
ReadBool takes anything but "false" as true ("True", "1", "yes" become true)
ReadInt returns 0 instead of the fallback for a value that is not a number
ReadList does not decode entities in list entries
Parse takes any XML-looking text for FluentFlyout's settings (loaded becomes true without <UserSettings>)
Parse defaults animationSpeed to 0 when FlyoutAnimationSpeed is missing (should be 2)
Parse reads filterMode from the wrong element (AppFilteringMode 1 gives filterMode 0)
Parse defaults hideCompletely to true when TaskbarWidgetHideCompletely is missing

context.title: tests/icon_pixels_test.cpp (the existing test: do not repeat it, add to it)

mutants.desc: IsGlyph counts pixels with alpha 47 (only alpha 48 and up should count)
IsGlyph allows a red difference of 25 from the first counted pixel (24 is the most allowed)
IsGlyph accepts 7 counted pixels (at least 8 are needed)
IsGlyph no longer accepts dark (black) glyphs
IsGlyph accepts a light but tinted colour whose channels are up to 63 apart, e.g. (255, 230, 200) (fewer than 24 apart is required)
Premultiply leaves pixels with alpha 254 unchanged
Premultiply rounds the red channel to nearest instead of down (red 1 at alpha 128 gives 1 instead of 0)
Shrink rounds the factor down (130 px wide with maxSide 64 gives factor 2 and 65 px instead of factor 3 and 44 px)
Shrink divides partial edge blocks by the full block size (f * f) instead of the pixels they have

context.title: tests/hwinfo_test.cpp (the existing test: do not repeat it, add to it)

mutants.desc: ParseTemperature accepts exactly -40 degrees C (more than -40 is required)
ParseTemperature accepts exactly 150 degrees C (less than 150 is required)
ParseTemperature converts Fahrenheit with 9/5 instead of 5/9
ParseTemperature reads the single character U+2103 (degree Celsius sign) as Fahrenheit
the number reader stops at a decimal comma ("52,4" reads as 52)
RankCpu gives rank 0 to an empty label when no preference is set (it should be -1)
RankCpu ranks a "Core Max" reading of a sensor that is not "CPU [..." as 5 (it should be -1)
PickCpu lets a later reading of the same rank replace an earlier one (the earlier one should stay)
PickCpu picks a well-ranked reading whose value is not a temperature (e.g. "CPU Package" = "65 W")
Judge counts a key exactly 20.0 s old as fresh without asking whether HWiNFO runs
Judge rejects values exactly 60.0 s old (60.0 is still usable)
Judge reports HWiNFO as running when the key holds no values
